# PKCS#12 (.pfx) import fixtures. Password for every store unless stated: tlslib
# Generated with OpenSSL 3.2.1 (multikey_pfx merged with JDK keytool). Do not weaken tests to fit these.
# Unless stated, every certificate is valid 2020-01-01..2126-09-15 UTC: re-issued with Go crypto over the original
# subject keys (same names, serials and extensions; the test CA got a new RSA-2048 key), then the
# stores were re-exported with OpenSSL 3.2.1 and JDK 21 keytool using the profiles below.
# rsa_pfx / ec_pfx: single self-signed leaf + its key, default profile
#   (PBES2 AES-256-CBC bags, SHA-256 integrity MAC).
# rsa_altalg_pfx: the same RSA leaf under a different profile (PBES2 AES-128-CBC bags,
#   SHA-1 MAC) - proves import is algorithm-independent, not pinned to one profile.
# chain_pfx: RSA leaf signed by a test root CA; store holds leaf key + leaf cert + CA cert.
# ca_cert_der: the test root CA certificate (DER), the PKIX anchor for chain_pfx.
# multikey_pfx: two private-key entries (rsa-leaf + ec-leaf); ambiguous for one credential.
# Leaf-selection fixtures (plaintext, no-MAC PFX - password is unused): TlsLib selects the leaf by
# key match, not by store order or the key<->cert link. They reuse chain_pfx's leaf + CA, so
# ca_cert_der stays the anchor. Provenance: extract chain_pfx's leaf, CA and (PKCS#8) key with
# OpenSSL, then reassemble as unencrypted no-MAC PFX SafeBags with the bag order and localKeyId
# below (asn1crypto) - OpenSSL cannot emit these arrangements. For the 2126 re-issue the leaf and
# CA DER were swapped into those same bags (Go); the bag layout and key bytes are unchanged.
# All expect chain [leaf, CA] except nomatch.
# nolink_cafirst_pfx: no localKeyId anywhere, CA bag first (positional linkage leads with the CA).
# orphanlink_pfx: the key's localKeyId matches no certificate (the linked lookup finds no leaf).
# wronglink_pfx: the key's localKeyId points at the CA certificate, not the leaf.
# nomatch_pfx: the key and the CA only - no certificate pairs the key (import must fail closed).
rsa_
rsa_altalg_
ec_
chain_
ca_cert_
multikey_

# Profile and encoding fixtures. All hold the rsa_pfx identity (self-signed leaf CN rsa.tlslib.test, valid
# 2020-01-01..2126-09-15, and its key; extracted from rsa_pfx with OpenSSL 3.6.1 and repacked), single
# leaf only because the test CA key is gone. Password tlslib unless stated. Inputs: leaf.key (PKCS#8 PEM),
# leaf.crt (PEM), written as leaf.key and leaf.crt in the commands below.
# legacy_pfx: OpenSSL 3.2.1 (Git for Windows, legacy provider) with
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -legacy -inkey leaf.key -in leaf.crt -name rsa-leaf -passout pass:tlslib
#   Certificate bag PBE-SHA1-RC2-40, key bag PBE-SHA1-3DES, SHA-1 MAC, 2048 iterations (OpenSSL 1.x profile).
# des3_pfx: OpenSSL 3.6.1 with
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -keypbe PBE-SHA1-3DES -certpbe PBE-SHA1-3DES -macalg sha1 -inkey leaf.key
#   -in leaf.crt -name rsa-leaf -passout pass:tlslib
#   Both bags pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC, SHA-1 MAC: the profile Windows documents as supported.
# pbmac1_pfx: OpenSSL 3.6.1 with
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -pbmac1_pbkdf2 -inkey leaf.key -in leaf.crt -name rsa-leaf -passout pass:tlslib
#   RFC 9579 PBMAC1 integrity (PBKDF2, HMAC-SHA-256), PBES2 AES-256-CBC bags, 2048 iterations.
# ed25519_pfx: self-signed Ed25519 leaf CN ed25519.tlslib.test (valid 2026-10-17..2126-09-23) made with OpenSSL 3.6.1:
#   openssl req -x509 -newkey ed25519 -nodes -keyout ed.key -out ed.crt -subj /CN=ed25519.tlslib.test -days 36500
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey ed.key -in ed.crt -name ed25519-leaf -passout pass:tlslib
#   Default profile (PBES2 AES-256-CBC, SHA-256 MAC). A key kind with no CNG signing path.
# utf8pw_pfx: OpenSSL 3.6.1 default profile (PBES2 AES-256-CBC, SHA-256 MAC) with a NON-ASCII password, NOT
#   tlslib: the UTF-8 bytes in utf8pw_password (63 61 66 c3a9 2d e697a5 e69cac: the letters c a f, U+00E9,
#   a hyphen, U+65E5 U+672C), written to a file with exactly those bytes and passed as
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey leaf.key -in leaf.crt -name rsa-leaf -passout file:pw8.txt
# nullpw_pfx: made on Windows 10 (19045) by a throwaway program that imports rsa_pfx with PFXImportCertStore
#   (PKCS12_NO_PERSIST_KEY, PKCS12_ALWAYS_CNG_KSP, CRYPT_EXPORTABLE; password tlslib) and exports the store with
#   PFXExportCertStoreEx(EXPORT_PRIVATE_KEYS, szPassword NULL), so the password is NULL, not empty. crypt32
#   writes its default profile (pbeWithSHA1And3-KeyTripleDES-CBC bags, SHA-1 MAC, 2000 iterations; the PBES2
#   export option answered ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED). Imports with an empty or absent password.
legacy_
des3_
pbmac1_
ed25519_
utf8pw_
utf8pw_password=636166c3a92de697a5e69cac
nullpw_
nolink_cafirst_
orphanlink_
wronglink_
nomatch_

# Hidden-key fixtures (plaintext, no-MAC PFX, so no password). Each holds the rsa_pfx identity (the self-signed leaf
# and its PKCS#8 key, both extracted from rsa_pfx) plus a second private-key bag with the ec_pfx key and no EC
# certificate. Built with a throwaway asn1crypto script, not committed (Pfx with one unencrypted SafeContents of SafeBags); localKeyId A = 0101,
# B = 0202. A store reader that pairs keys with certificates by public key drops the EC key; one that counts key
# bags keeps it. Bag order is always cert, rsa key, ec key.
# hid_nolink_pfx: cert(A), rsa key(A), ec key without localKeyId.
# hid_orphan_pfx: cert(A), rsa key(A), ec key(B), where B matches no certificate.
# hid_sharedlink_pfx: cert(A), rsa key(A), ec key(A), both keys naming the one certificate.
hid_nolink_
hid_orphan_
hid_sharedlink_

# Key-pairing fixtures (OpenSSL 3.6.1, default profile: PBES2 AES-256-CBC, SHA-256 MAC, password tlslib).
# pss_pfx: self-signed leaf CN rsapss.tlslib.test (valid 2026-10-17..2126-09-23) whose key is
#   id-RSASSA-PSS (RFC 4055), no chain:
#   openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa-pss -pkeyopt rsa_keygen_bits:2048 -pkeyopt rsa_pss_keygen_md:sha256
#   -pkeyopt rsa_pss_keygen_saltlen:32 -nodes -keyout pss.key -out pss.crt -subj /CN=rsapss.tlslib.test -days 36500
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey pss.key -in pss.crt -name pss-leaf -passout pass:tlslib
pss_

# Unsupported-key fixtures (plaintext, no-MAC PFX, so no password), built like the hid_* stores with a throwaway
# asn1crypto script, not committed. The DSA key (DSA-2048, OpenSSL 3.6.1 genpkey, PKCS#8) is a key this library cannot sign with;
# dsa.tlslib.test (valid 2026-10-17..2126-09-23) is its self-signed certificate; localKeyId A = 0101.
# unsupp_pfx: cert(A) and the DSA key(A) alone.
# unsupp_multikey_pfx: the rsa_pfx leaf cert(A) and its key(A), then the DSA key with no localKeyId and no certificate.
unsupp_
unsupp_multikey_

# dupkey_pfx (OpenSSL 3.6.1, default profile, password tlslib): two self-signed certificates, both CN
# rsa.tlslib.test, over the one rsa_pfx key (leaf.key). leaf2.crt (serial 2, valid 2026-10-17..2126-09-23) has the
# lower DER; the store links the key to leaf.crt (the rsa_pfx leaf), the higher DER, which is dupkey_linked_cert:
#   openssl req -x509 -new -key leaf.key -subj /CN=rsa.tlslib.test -set_serial 2 -days 36500 -out leaf2.crt
#   openssl pkcs12 -export -inkey leaf.key -in leaf.crt -certfile leaf2.crt -name rsa-leaf -passout pass:tlslib
dupkey_
dupkey_linked_

# secp256k1 fixtures (plaintext, no-MAC PFX, so no password), built like unsupp_* with a throwaway asn1crypto script.
# The key is a secp256k1 PKCS#8 key (OpenSSL 3.6.1 ecparam + pkcs8 -topk8): a curve this library cannot sign with.
# k1_multikey_pfx: the rsa_pfx leaf cert(A) and its key(A), then the secp256k1 key with no localKeyId and no certificate.
# k1_nocert_pfx: the rsa_pfx leaf cert(A) and the secp256k1 key alone, so no certificate pairs the key.
k1_multikey_
k1_nocert_
